  • 💥 High Damage Output: Capable of delivering up to 8 wounds to tough targets like vehicles, while slaying around 5-6 guardsmen on average.
  • 🛡️ Unique Curse: Defeating him in a duel could lead to a painful transformation into Lucius, adding a menacing layer to encounters.

📊 Important Numerical Insights

  • 📈 Movement: 8 inches base movement allows for strategic positioning.
  • 🔪 Damage Potential: 6 attacks at strength 8 with AP-3 and damage 3 against elite units.
  • ⚔️ Attack Rolls: 10 attacks at strength 4 with AP-1 and damage 1 against infantry, ensuring flexibility in combat.
  • 💔 Durability: 6 wounds with a 2+ save and a 5+ Feel No Pain means he can withstand significant damage before going down.

item.title: How to Beat a Unit You CAN'T DESTROY - Ideas and Tactics
item.description: The video provides strategies for managing high-cost units in Warhammer 40K, emphasizing the importance of understanding threats, utilizing battlefield terrain, focusing on objectives, and ensuring proper army composition to effectively deal with powerful enemies.
item.content:encoded:
📢 Managing Big Scary Units in Warhammer 40K

📝 Summary

  • 🔥 Understanding Threats: Learn how to deal with high investment units that can dominate the battlefield, such as Magnus, Angron, and Katan shards.
  • ⚔️ Basic Strategies: Employ tactics like ignoring the big threats, playing the mission, baiting the enemy, and counterattacking.
  • 🛡️ Unit Characteristics: High-cost units (300+ points) often have weaknesses; for example, Magnus has great damage but isn't indestructible.
  • 🌍 Terrain Matters: The layout of the battlefield can greatly affect how you handle these units, particularly with dense terrain vs open spaces.
  • 📊 Army Composition: Ensure your army list includes options for dealing with tanks and heavy units to avoid being overwhelmed.
  • 🎯 Focus on Objectives: Sometimes it's more effective to ignore powerful enemy units and focus on scoring points instead.

📊 Important Numerical Insights

  • 🔢 Point Costs: Many high investment units are around 300 points or more, making them significant threats on the battlefield.
  • 📈 Unit Efficiency: Units like Magnus cost approximately 450 points, requiring careful consideration of whether to engage or ignore.
  • ⏳ Turns of Impact: High investment units can only significantly impact the game for 5 turns, emphasizing the importance of damage mitigation.

❓ Questions to Consider

  • 🤔 How do you decide when to engage a high-cost unit versus ignoring it and focusing on objectives?
  • 💭 What strategies have you found most effective in dealing with units that seem impossible to kill?
  • 🧐 In your experience, how does terrain influence the effectiveness of big scary units in Warhammer 40K?
